transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because people keep saying the foreclosure is just… paperwork, missed payments, whatever. But that’s not what’s happening. The bank, the loan servicer, even some people at my job—they’ve been working together quietly to push me out of my house. I’ve been seeing it for almost two years, and the papers they keep showing me don’t change that.

Over these past two years, have you also noticed significant changes in your mood—like periods of feeling unusually elevated, energetic, or irritable, or on the other hand, feeling very down, hopeless, or losing interest in things?
I don’t know. I mean… I’ve been stressed, obviously. Anyone would be. But I haven’t really been tracking my mood like that.
Besides your certainty about the plot against you, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things others don't, or other unusual sensory experiences?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed anything like that. It’s not voices or seeing things, it’s just… what’s been happening.
Do you have any medical conditions—like a neurological illness, head injury, or other health problems—or do you use any substances or medications that could be affecting your thinking?
I don’t really have anything to point to. No major health thing that I know of. I’m not sure what would count as affecting my thinking.
Have you noticed any recent problems with your memory, concentration, or feeling confused or disoriented at times?
Not really… I mean, I get distracted sometimes, but I think that’s just from stress. I don’t feel confused or anything.
Did anything happen physically around the time these beliefs started two years ago—like an illness, injury, surgery, or starting a new medication—that you can recall?
I can’t really think of anything like that. Nothing physical that stands out to me from then.
Aside from your concerns about the foreclosure plot, how have things been going for you in other areas—like your job performance, relationships, and daily routine?

Mostly okay, I guess. I still go to work, supervise people, do the schedules, deal with customers… all of that. I take care of myself.

It’s more when something connects to the house—mail, calls from the bank, certain paperwork at work—that things get… harder. Then I start paying attention to it.
Have you experienced any headaches, dizziness, seizures, weakness, or changes in coordination or balance over the past couple of years?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, nothing like seizures or balance problems. I get normal aches sometimes, but nothing that seems connected or unusual.
Do you currently use alcohol, marijuana, or any other recreational drugs, and if so, how often?
No… not really. I might have a drink once in a while, but I don’t use drugs or anything like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief (conspiracy involving bank, loan servicer, and coworkers to force him out of his house) persisting for approximately two years. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech, no negative symptoms, and no mood episode symptoms reported (no mania/depression tracked or endorsed). Functioning outside the delusional theme remains largely intact—he continues to work, supervise staff, and manage daily responsibilities, with only situational distress when delusion-related stimuli occur (mail, bank calls). No evidence of substance use, medical/neurological cause, or cognitive impairment. This clinical picture—an isolated, persistent, non-bizarre delusion with preserved functioning and absence of other psychotic or mood symptoms—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22) rather than Schizophrenia (F20, which requires broader psychotic symptoms and functional decline) or Mood Disorder with psychotic features (F30, which requires mood episode criteria).
